Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. Our security and procurement teams are consolidating evidence for our review of Redwood Dedicated/Private deployments. To finalize our technical assessment we need the following artifacts and clarifications: 

- Network isolation diagrams for both Dedicated and Private deployment modes (including edge components, bastion/jump hosts, and any customer-managed on-prem connectors).
- A mapping matrix that shows which workloads/components are co-tenanted versus customer-dedicated, and where KMS boundaries are enforced (customer keys vs. Redwood-managed).
- Egress controls and outbound firewall rules (how IP allowlists, NAT, and egress flow are enforced from tenant workloads).
- Evidence pointers for SOC 2 (system boundaries, crypto/KMS), and SIG/CAIQ answers where architecture diagrams are relevant.
- A brief note on what is redacted for IP reasons and what we can expect as downloadable artifacts (redacted diagrams are fine).

Attached is a short version of our questionnaire to help you prioritize (Delta_Security_Questionnaire_Shortlist.pdf). Can you confirm what you can provide this week and an estimate for redacted diagrams + a full evidence bundle (SOC 2 excerpts, CAIQ/SIG responses)?

We may have follow-ups around KMS separation and cross-tenant egress; it would be great to have an infra/security engineer on the call if needed. Are you available for a 30-minute sync on Thursday (12/3) morning PT?

Thanks,
Maria Gonzalez
Senior InfoSec Engineer

Maria — following up with the clarifications you asked for. Mina and Jonas provided the technical notes below; I consolidated and attached the redacted diagrams and the egress/KMS mapping.

Attachments in this reply: redwood_private_isolation_v2.pdf (redacted topology), egress_kms_mapping.csv (tabular mapping of egress patterns and KMS ownership), soc2_scope_matrix.xlsx (SOC 2 control excerpts relevant to architecture).

Short answers up front: 
- Bastion/jump host: In Dedicated mode, bastion hosts are provisioned per-customer pool by default (not shared across customer pools). For Hosted-mode customers we operate a shared bastion fleet behind strict RBAC and session recording.
- Private (VPC) egress: For Private deployments placed inside a customer VPC, egress (NAT, internet gateway) is customer-managed unless the customer requests Redwood-managed egress (managed egress is available as an add-on and will be explicitly noted in the controls). In Dedicated (Redwood-managed) deployments, egress exits through our managed egress gateway; egress IPs can be static and added to your allowlists.
- KMS separation: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) for sensitive data at rest. The mapping in egress_kms_mapping.csv shows which artifacts support CMKs and which use Redwood-managed keys; for CMKs we provide guidance on HSM-backed KMS and key-rotation policies and will provide a scoped SOC 2 excerpt showing the control owner and process.

Quoted internal notes (for audit trail):

On Thu, Dec 3, 2026 at 09:18 AM Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Bastion design: dedicated pools get customer-isolated bastion hosts. Access is via short-lived certs issued by our internal CA; sessions are recorded and stored per-tenant with RBAC-based retention controls.
> 
> Key management: for CMK requests we hand off the KMS ARN mapping and provide an integration checklist; Redwood maintains a separate encryption keyspace for platform metadata that is never exposed to customer CMKs.

On Thu, Dec 3, 2026 at 09:22 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Egress: Private (in-customer VPC) = customer-controlled routing by default. Managed egress option = Redwood-managed egress gateway with per-tenant SNAT and egress allowlist. Managed egress includes flow logs and per-tenant egress audit entries.

Next steps: 
- I uploaded the artifacts to the Drive folder and added the mapping spreadsheets. Please confirm receipt and whether you want the unredacted diagrams under an NDA — we can route that via our security team and a short redaction plan.
- If helpful, we can move to a short technical call next week to walk the diagrams (I kept Thu 12/3 in case you want the original slot; otherwise propose Mon 12/7).

Thanks,
